title: RIS grouped/low-rank Mirror phase control screen
hypothesis: Across synthetic cascaded single-user links, a two-coordinate phase View can preserve most of continuous RIS beamforming quality using fewer controller bits than full native per-element phase programming.
scope: Ideal narrowband 64-element RIS simulator; not PA290 reproduction, 3GPP model or hardware measurement.

channels.cascaded_coefficients: unit-magnitude spatial phase ramp with randomized slope/curvature and per-element phase noise; direct complex path

serialization.format: custom fixed-header packed inference command stream; per-element/group/rank codes bit-packed with scenario ordering and decoder metadata included
serialization.authority: actual serialized inference control payload bytes

success_gate: Mirror retains >=95% of continuous upper mean rate in every fresh world and uses <=50% actual packed command bytes versus native full-element 2-bit phase control.
failure_gate: Any fresh world misses quality/bytes gate, or native two-coordinate phase-gradient control exactly aliases Mirror.
boundaries: No multi-user sum-rate, AP/RIS joint optimizer, RF/phase-switch energy, settling latency, fabrication or measured channel claim.
Controller counts are proxies, not hardware energy or latency.
